name: Vernal-Hoodoo
description: A single unbroken ocean swallows the horizon, its color shifting from wine-dark deeps to bright shelf-teal. The only interruptions are acid rain regions, breaking the swell in a ragged arc.
The air carries burnt sugar and sulfur, and sound behaves strangely: footsteps crack loud, then die without echo. At night the temperature drops fast enough to hear the rock tick as it contracts.
Geologists argue about the strata here: several layers appear deposited out of order, as if the planet's history were shuffled like cards.
There is money in biomass here, and history in the rocks, and the two keep interfering with each other. Mediators do brisk business at inflated rates.
